land.text: Córdoba and its vicinity, where the aristocracy ended the caliphate with the overthrow of Hisham III in 1031

predecessors.note: Cliopatria draws the Caliphate of Córdoba row to 1071 (564.7 thousand km2 at its largest); from 1034 its shape (9,813 km2) is this state, as the caliphate-of-cordoba dossier's keyframe_review for 1034 and 1066 says, and no Jahwarid row exists.

land.text: Córdoba, captured in 1070 by al-Mu'tamid of Seville

successors.note: Seville lost Córdoba from 1075 to 1078 (Taifa of Córdoba page); the Almoravids took it in 1091 (the infobox's end of the taifa).

rulers.name: Abu al-Hazm Jahwar ibn Muhammad
rulers.note: 'Abū 'l-Ḥazm led Córdoba from 1031 until his death in 1043'.

rulers.name: Abu al-Walid Muhammad ibn Jahwar
rulers.note: Page: governed 'twenty-one years' after 1043 (so to about 1064), later delegating to his sons Abd al-Rahman and Abd al-Malik.

rulers.name: Abd al-Malik ibn Jahwar
rulers.note: The page gives no start; he stripped his brother of authority and was deposed in 1070. The start is the end of his father's twenty-one years (reading).

correction.text: Córdoba and its vicinity: 'the Cordoban aristocracy created a council to govern the city'; the page lists the territory as Córdoba and its vicinity and mentions neither Jaén nor Écija. Drawn as the Córdoba-sized shape that Cliopatria keeps under the Caliphate of Córdoba row for 1034-1071 (9,813 km2) and that the caliphate-of-cordoba dossier marks 'wrong' and hands to the Taifa of Córdoba (the Jahwarid republic) 1031-1069

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Jahwarid row. Its Caliphate of Córdoba shapes of 1034-1065 (9,813 km2, bbox -5.82..-3.97 E, 37.38..38.55 N) and 1066-1071 (9,788 km2, same bbox) are the Córdoba rump, not a wider Hammudid-era realm; the caliphate-of-cordoba dossier marks both 'wrong' with the correction 'the same shape, to be drawn as the Taifa of Córdoba (the Jahwarid republic) 1031-1069' and lists this state as the successor. The Taifa of Córdoba page (re-read 2026-10-25) gives no area, no infobox area and no town beyond Córdoba itself ('Córdoba and its vicinity'; Jaén, Écija, Carmona and Almodóvar are not mentioned), so the page cannot size the vicinity; the only extent on record is Cliopatria's shape, which agrees with the neighbour dossier, and it is used as it stands (drawn about 9,800 km2, ratio 1.0 to Cliopatria). An earlier draft drew a 35 km circle (about 3,850 km2) on the false premise that the Cliopatria shapes were a wider realm; that reading is withdrawn. The shape covers 1031-1033 too, although Cliopatria's 1028-1033 shape (15,032 km2) was larger: its western Beja strip is not on this page (see notes). The Seville dossier books the whole province of Córdoba in 1070, a larger reading than this shape.

ledger.note: 1031: Córdoba becomes a republic under the Jahwarids once the caliphate falls. Infobox 'Córdoba organized into a republic: 1031'; 'Abū 'l-Ḥazm led Córdoba from 1031 until his death in 1043'; the Hisham III page: 'After the Caliphate fell with the overthrow of Hisham III in 1031' (Sa'id was killed on 30 November 1031).

1070: 'In 1070, after defeating the Toledan army, al-Mu'tamid captured Córdoba and deposed 'Abd al-Malik', who was imprisoned and exiled to Saltés. The infobox dates the exile of the Córdoban ruler to 1091.
1070: the Jahwarid republic ends; 'Seville lost control of Córdoba from 1075 to 1078' and kept it until 1091.

wars.name: Seville's conquest of Córdoba
wars.outcome: Al-Mu'tamid of Seville defeated the Toledan army and captured Córdoba in 1070, deposing Abd al-Malik.
wars.note: The page mentions a Toledan siege without a date.

certainty.note: City-state: 'Córdoba and its vicinity' with no boundary on the page.

sources.title: Taifa of Córdoba
sources.note: Republic of 1031, Jahwar 1031-1043, Muhammad 21 years, Abd al-Malik, conquest 1070, Seville lost it 1075-1078, taifa ended 1091; territory Córdoba and its vicinity; no area, no 30 November 1031. Re-read 2026-10-25 for the extent: infobox has no area field; text says only 'Córdoba and its vicinity'; Jaén, Écija, Carmona and Almodóvar are not mentioned; the fetch tool rendered the infobox heading as 'Taifa Republic of Córdoba, c. 1037', against 1031 in the infobox body and the text.

sources.title: Hisham III
sources.note: Overthrow in 1031 (Sa'id killed 30 November 1031), the aristocracy's council; no mention of Jahwar. The Caliphate_of_Córdoba page was opened first and returned only a maintenance banner.

notes: Written for eu-12-x (asked for by eu-12-h as the first period of taifa-of-cordoba, 1031-1070); two pages plus the Caliphate page that returned a banner only. The slug taifa-of-cordoba is the Cliopatria row (1147-1249, a different, later state), so this dossier uses jahwarid-taifa-of-cordoba; the Seville dossier books its 1070 gain with counterpart taifa-of-cordoba, which a reconciler should map here. Conflicts: the end is 1070 (the capture and deposition, text) or 1091 (infobox), the latter being the end of Seville's hold; Abd al-Malik's accession and Muhammad's reign (21 years from 1043) are the page's own and no second page was opened to check them. Not settled: the territory beyond the city; the page does not mention Jaén or Écija. Gazetteer: Córdoba is a place in Spain. Repair 2026-10-25 (reviewer finding on the keyframe): the 35 km circle (about 3,850 km2) is replaced by Cliopatria's Caliphate of Córdoba shape of 1034 (9,813 km2) in the keyframe, the found, loss and dissolve events, the war zone and both neighbours' land. The earlier note that Cliopatria's 1031-1071 shapes were 'a wider (Hammudid-era) realm' was wrong: they are the Córdoba rump that the caliphate-of-cordoba dossier hands to this state (verdict 'wrong', correction 'the same shape, to be drawn as the Taifa of Córdoba 1031-1069'). The page itself still gives no area, so the shape is Cliopatria's reading, accepted because the neighbour dossier agrees. Open: Cliopatria's 1028-1033 shape (15,032 km2) included a Beja strip in the west; the caliphate-of-cordoba dossier says it left the rump in 1033 (Taifa of Mértola), and no page opened says who held it from December 1031 to 1033; this dossier draws the 1034 shape from 1031. The taifa-of-seville 1070 gain names the whole province of Córdoba (larger than this shape) with counterpart taifa-of-cordoba, to be mapped to this slug.
